original_question: Can one develop a theory of general fractional integrals and general fractional derivatives on conventional function spaces beyond the spaces treated in the paper, in particular on L^p spaces and on Holder weighted spaces?
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, Open Problem 9, read in the precise framework of Section 2.3 (especially Definitions 2–3 and Theorems 8–9) on general fractional integrals and derivatives with Sonine-type kernels on the positive real semi-axis.
correct_elements: Your draft points to the correct open problem and is already very close to the paper’s wording. It correctly identifies that the issue is to extend the theory of GFIs/GFDs beyond the function spaces already treated, and it names exactly the two example classes explicitly mentioned in the paper: L_p spaces and Hölder weighted spaces.
missing_details: The paper is not asking about fractional operators in general, but about the specific GFIs and GFDs introduced in Section 2.3.
The domain is the positive real semi-axis R_+=(0,∞); finite intervals and the whole line R are separated out as Open Problem 8 and should not be merged into Problem 9.
The relevant operators are the arbitrary-order GFI and GFDs from Definition 3, attached to a kernel pair (κ,k) in L_n for some n in N.
The hidden kernel assumptions are κ in C_{-1}(0,∞), k in C_{-1,0}(0,∞), and (κ∗k)(t)=h_n(t)=t^(n-1)/(n-1)! for t>0.
Both derivative types are intended: the Riemann–Liouville-type operator D(k) and the Caputo-type operator *D(k), together with the integral operator I(κ).
The draft does not say that the current theory in the paper is developed on C_{-1}(0,∞) and related C_{-1}-based image/regularity spaces appearing in Theorems 5, 6, 8, and 9.

To make the question stand-alone, one should indicate what counts as 'develop a theory': in the nearby context this means extending the mapping/inverse/fundamental-theorem framework established in Section 2.3.

There are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or 'for all sufficiently large m' parameters here; the hidden parameters that matter are n, the kernel pair (κ,k), the domain (0,∞), and the target function space.
refined_question: Let n be a positive integer and let (κ,k) be a pair of kernels in L_n on R_+=(0,∞), so that κ in C_{-1}(0,∞), k in C_{-1,0}(0,∞), and (κ∗k)(t)=h_n(t)=t^(n-1)/(n-1)! for t>0. For the associated arbitrary-order general fractional integral and general fractional derivatives from Section 2.3, namely (I(κ)f)(t)=∫_0^t κ(t−τ)f(τ)dτ, (D(k)f)(t)=d^n/dt^n ∫_0^t k(t−τ)f(τ)dτ, and (*D(k)f)(t)=D(k)(f−Σ_{j=0}^{n-1} f^(j)(0)h_{j+1})(t), can one develop on other conventional function spaces—specifically L_p spaces and Hölder weighted spaces—a theory analogous to the one proved on the C_{-1}-based spaces in Section 2.3, including the appropriate mapping properties and counterparts of the first and second fundamental theorems for these operators?
justification: The draft is closest to Open Problem 9 because its wording is nearly the same as the paper’s official statement. The nearby context in Section 2.3 fixes the exact operators under discussion: first the Sonine-kernel setting on C_{-1}-type spaces (Definition 1, Theorems 5–6), and then the arbitrary-order setting via kernel pairs (κ,k) in L_n (Definition 2, Definition 3, Theorems 8–9). That context supplies the domain, kernel hypotheses, operator formulas, and the kind of structure already proved. Open Problem 8 separately asks for finite-interval and whole-line versions, so a paper-faithful refinement of Problem 9 must stay on the positive semi-axis and ask specifically for an extension of the Section 2.3 theory to L_p and Hölder weighted spaces, rather than broadening to other domains or other kinds of fractional operators.
